sources.page_title: "The Wall" Canadian CD Columbia C2K 36183 and Pre-Emphasis | Steve Hoffman Music Forums
sources.full_text:
I gave up on the West German Harvest black face order from Macedonia and asked for and received a refund. I then bought this disc set from a seller in Germany and had to here in California in 7 days. Note: US buyers should not order from Eastern Europe unless you are prepared to wait a long time and possibly not receive the order at all. 
 
 I used SoX to de-emphasize the tracks from the Canadian version (C2K-36183) of the original Sony Japan mastering and compared it to both the "Shine On" mastering and the West German Harvest black face mastering. All three sound good, but I definitely prefer the West German Harvest black face mastering. It is more natural sounding and has better dynamics than the other two.

sources.page_title: "The Wall" Canadian CD Columbia C2K 36183 and Pre-Emphasis | Steve Hoffman Music Forums
sources.full_text:
Folks, I have what the Pink Floyd Archives would call the Canadian "Columbia Records 3rd issue". Here is the link: 
 
 Pink Floyd Archives-Canadian CD Discography 
 
 The CDs labels are back as shown here: 
 
 
 
 I wanted to rip these CDs to play on my Roon-based 2 channel setup in my home. 
 
 My issue is that both the latest version of EAC and the "drutil" in macOS High Sierra show the tracks having pre-emphasis according to the TOC of the disks. The Pink Floyd Archives do not show this CD as having pre-emphasis. Other "The Wall" CDs known to have pre-emphasis are listed as having it. See here: 
 
 Pink Floyd Archives-Japanese Pink Floyd CD Discography 
 
 So, I sent en email off to Vernon at the Pink Floyd Archives noting that I thought his data may be incorrect on the above CDs. He wrote back telling me that the EAC was wrong. At the time of my writing him, I had not use the "drutil" in macOS to check for pre-emphasis. So that information was not included. I have since followed up but have not heard back yet. 
 
 So, does this Canadian release of "The Wall" actually have pre-emphasis as the CDs TOC indicate or is the TOC in error? 
 
 Thanks!

sources.author: Randy W
sources.excerpt: To me (on my system and in my listening room) the BT is much more relaxed sounding than the 2009. It is also "crankable", meaning it is not compressed in the least - it remains sonically superior at louder listening levels compared to the 2009. This is my major problem with the stereo remasters in general. Wouldn't want to be without it personally.
sources.page_title: Which is the best-sounding Abbey Road CD? | Steve Hoffman Music Forums
sources.full_text: To me (on my system and in my listening room) the BT is much more relaxed sounding than the 2009. It is also "crankable", meaning it is not compressed in the least - it remains sonically superior at louder listening levels compared to the 2009. This is my major problem with the stereo remasters in general. The BT is not hyper detailed, but all the details on the 2009 are there - just subtler and more integrated into the mix. Wouldn't want to be without it personally.
